scenarios.title: Explain a checkout bug to a developer
scenarios.context: You’re in a team stand-up. You found a reproducible problem on the checkout page. Explain what happens, how you reproduced it, and what you expected instead.
scenarios.colleaguePrompt: Hi Anna, I saw your ticket about checkout. Can you walk me through the issue and tell me what happens after the user clicks Pay?
scenarios.sampleResponse: The checkout page crash when I click Pay. Yesterday I reproduce the issue on Chrome and Safari. The user see an error message, and the payment don't go through. I expected the order to complete, but the page stay on loading.

simulatedFeedback.opening: Your explanation is understandable and includes the trigger, impact, and expected behaviour.

items.title: Recurring pattern detected: verb forms
items.copy: This pattern has now appeared 7 times across recent practice scenarios. Prioritise a short review before the next conversation.
pairs: The page stays on the loading screen

items.title: More precise system-state language
items.copy: Your meaning is clear. More precise QA language could make the report easier to act on.
pairs: the loading spinner remains visible / the page remains stuck in a loading state

items.title: Make the report easy to scan
items.copy: Try structuring the explanation as: Steps to reproduce → Actual result → Expected result.

scenarios.title: Report a file-upload issue
scenarios.context: A user uploads a PDF larger than 10 MB. The progress bar reaches 100%, but the file never appears in the document list. Explain the problem to a developer and say what you expected to happen.
scenarios.sampleResponse: When the user uploads a PDF larger than 10 MB, the progress bar reaches 100%, but the file does not appear in the document list. I reproduced the issue twice in Chrome. I expected the file to appear after the upload completed.

practiceActivities.title: Verb Forms for Reporting Software Issues
practiceActivities.description: Practise the verb forms you need to describe reproducible software behaviour clearly.
practiceActivities.passThresholdNote: Illustrative threshold for this prototype; not empirically validated.

items.instruction: You are writing the Actual result of a reproducible bug. Choose the correct verb form.
items.stem: Actual result: The discount code ___ after the page reloads.
items.feedback: Reproducible behaviour is described in the present simple, and ‘the discount code’ is singular, so the verb takes -s. The past simple would describe one past event, not a bug that happens every time.

items.instruction: In stand-up, you explain what you did yesterday to reproduce a bug.
items.stem: Yesterday I ___ the bug on staging and attached the logs to the ticket.
items.feedback: ‘Yesterday’ marks finished time, so a completed action takes the past simple, like ‘attached’ in the same sentence. The present perfect does not combine with finished-time words such as ‘yesterday’.

items.instruction: One part of this Actual result needs correcting. Which change is needed?
items.stem: “When the user clicks Save, the form don’t show an error, but the changes aren’t stored.”
items.feedback: ‘The form’ is singular, so the negative is ‘doesn’t show’. ‘The changes’ is plural, so ‘aren’t stored’ is already correct, and ‘the user clicks’ is correct present simple.

items.instruction: A developer will act on this ticket. Which description is both accurate and clearest?
items.stem: Choose the best description of the issue.
options: When the user applies a discount code, the total does not update, and the original price is charged.
When the user apply a discount code, the total don’t update, and the original price is charged.
There is a problem with the discount code, it is not working correctly at checkout sometimes.
items.answer: When the user applies a discount code, the total does not update, and the original price is charged.
items.feedback: The first option names the trigger (‘applies’), the actual result (‘does not update’) and the impact, with accurate verb forms. The second has the same content but two verb-form errors; the third is grammatical but too vague to reproduce.

items.instruction: Complete the Actual result for a reproducible bug. Write the correct form of each verb in brackets.
items.answer: taps · generates · doesn’t start (or does not start)
items.feedback: Present simple throughout: this is reproducible behaviour. Singular subjects take -s (‘taps’, ‘generates’), and the negative uses ‘doesn’t’ / ‘does not’ + base form (‘start’).
items.validationNote: Checked against a fixed list of accepted answers — not free-text analysis.
